fit.gap_handling_summary: The outputs present strong production NLP, Azure, serving and monitoring evidence without inflating the personal RAG demo. Five-plus years of overall experience is supported, but only about three years and eight months in the explicitly documented production ML-engineer role is established as of November 2026; the bank role does not establish additional production-shipping tenure. CI/CD, automated testing, data versioning, orchestration, ingestion-pipeline ownership and cost evaluation remain unproven. The documents generally show the nearest genuine experience rather than inventing missing qualifications.

issues: The summary is somewhat long and could prioritise production NLP, Azure and customer-service relevance more sharply.
The four-year production-ML requirement is not established by the documented chronology, although the CV does not falsely claim that it is.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in sensible order with intact names, tools, dates and bullets.
Strong coverage of Python, Azure, MLflow, production serving, monitoring and transformer fine-tuning.
RAG is represented by the expanded retrieval-augmented project title, but the literal acronym appears only in the cover letter.
Evaluation, text datasets and customer support are represented semantically through metrics, annotated documents and customer-service reporting.
TF-IDF provides genuine feature-engineering evidence, but that explicit keyword is absent.
Several production-engineering keywords are missing because the source material does not establish them.
A strict four-year production-ML screening rule could reject the application despite the broader five-plus-year experience statement.

issues: The opening sentence carries the degree, overall tenure, production experience and PhD in one long sentence.
Much of the middle repeats CV metrics and tools; a more selective account could make the contribution to merchant-support workflows clearer.
The letter does not establish the missing production tenure or engineering practices, although it correctly avoids inventing them.
strengths: Names the correct company and exact role.
Connects customer-complaint classification to customer-service work.
Uses grounded production scale, evaluation and monitoring results.
Explicitly identifies the RAG work as a personal, non-production prototype.
Uses the company's documented ownership, context-sharing and learning culture.
Correctly replaces the earlier letter's outdated employer and local-job framing.

spacing_issues: CV page one is relatively dense, while page two is only 53.5% filled, leaving a substantial lower blank area.
consistency_issues: The first employment date is right-aligned beside the role, while the next two employment dates sit on separate left-aligned lines.
issues: The long first-page summary and several multi-line bullets slightly slow scanning.
Both documents otherwise use compatible serif typography, readable 11-point body text and clean margins; no clipping or overlap is visible.

fluency_and_tone_issues: "experimentation tracking" is understandable but less idiomatic than "experiment tracking".
"I hold an MSc ... and have over five years ... and I am currently pursuing a PhD" is an overloaded opening sentence.

parsed.summary: Both documents are accurate, professional and well targeted to production NLP and customer-support AI, with particularly strong deployment, monitoring and dataset-quality evidence. They correctly preserve the unfinished PhD and the non-production status of the RAG demo, without inventing cloud platforms, engineering practices or relocation commitments. The main limitation is substantive fit: four years of production ML-engineer experience is not established, and CI/CD, testing, data versioning and ingestion-pipeline ownership remain unproven. The PDFs are readable and parse cleanly, although the CV has uneven page density and the letter could reduce repetition.
